questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Custom Form Controls”?
options: Custom Form Controls means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Custom Form Controls removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “ControlValueAccessor” in this lesson?
options: Assume “ControlValueAccessor” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “ControlValueAccessor” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “ControlValueAccessor” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.

questions.answer_key: Connect “ControlValueAccessor” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “ControlValueAccessor” under Custom Form Controls. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Custom Form Controls”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
